title: Sima de los Huesos
summary: Sima de los Huesos is a deep chamber in the Atapuerca cave complex in northern Spain. It yielded fossils of about 28 early humans, dated to roughly 430,000 years ago. DNA from them shows they were early Neanderthal-line people, which pushed back the date by which Neanderthals and Denisovans had split.

uncertainty.note: Wikipedia (GA) reports layered dating from about 396,000 to 448,000 years; about 430,000 is the central figure. Tolerance is the editor's rounding, not a source value.

where.modern_name: Atapuerca, near Burgos, Castilla y León, Spain

importance.justification: Largest single-site sample of Middle Pleistocene humans, with DNA tying them to the Neanderthal lineage.

sources.title: DNA and the first Neanderthals
sources.publisher: Smithsonian Institution, National Museum of Natural History
